title: [claude draft] The Emperor's New Clothes (Andersen, 1837)
note: Claude draft, not Nandu's final script. Narration is exactly as drafted. Tags are Claude's own tagging, so the score tests the tagging, not the script. Historical facts are not yet checked against sources.
logline: An emperor parades in invisible clothes until a child says what everyone sees.
narration: Once there was an emperor who loved new clothes more than his people. Two swindlers arrive. They promise cloth so fine only clever people can see it. They set up empty looms and work all day. The emperor sends his minister to look. The minister sees nothing. But he is afraid to say so. He praises the cloth. Everyone does the same. On parade day, the emperor walks through the street in his new clothes. The crowd cheers, because no one wants to look foolish. Then a small child says it plainly: he has nothing on. A whisper spreads. Then the whole crowd says it. The emperor shivers, but he walks on, head high, to the end. The story is nearly two hundred years old. The lesson is the same: one honest voice can break a silence.
